tagline.text: A quiet 1 km stretch of sand and sunsets on Puerto Princesa's west coast

location.label: Location
location.text: West coast of Puerto Princesa City, Palawan, about 30 km northwest of downtown

best_season.label: Best time to visit
best_season.text: January–May dry season (check wave conditions locally)

budget.label: Budget
budget.text: About ₱500~5,000 (per person, from public transport and meals up to a shared private van)

children.text: Nagtabon Beach is a quiet beach about 1 km long on the west coast, roughly 30 km from downtown Puerto Princesa. With no hotels or resorts, only local cottages and eateries, it feels simple, and it works well for a half day that combines sunset, a motorbike ride and a boat trip to Chicken Island.
Nagtabon Beach lies on the west coast of Puerto Princesa City on Palawan Island. It is about
31 km
from downtown (guides give figures between 30 and 34 km) and is described as roughly
1 km

long. Unlike the island-hopping trips of Honda Bay to the east or the Underground River tour to the north, it is not a place where tour buses arrive, and on weekdays many visitors report seeing only a few local families, fishermen and playing children. The sea faces the West Philippine Sea (the South China Sea side).

The beach's biggest appeal is that it feels undeveloped. There are no upscale resorts or large facilities, only cottages, small eateries and a few bungalows run by locals along the shore. Travel blogs candidly say that the sand is not especially white and the coral is not colorful. On the other hand, some describe the entry point as having few rocks or algae and soft sand that is easy on the feet. So rather than expecting the dazzling scenery of Boracay or El Nido, think of it as a place to go within an hour of the city and rest quietly.

Transport is the biggest factor in choosing this beach. The beach lies on a road that branches west off the northern national highway out of the city. Guides say it takes about 40~50 minutes by motorbike and about 50 minutes by van. By public transport, the known route is to take a bus from San Jose Terminal toward El Nido, Sabang or Roxas, get off at Bacungan and switch to a tricycle. A rental car, motorbike or chartered van makes the trip much easier.

Puerto Princesa is one of the largest cities in the Philippines by area, so even getting from the city center to the beach feels like going to another district. According to Wikipedia, the Underground River National Park alone is about
50 km

from downtown. Nagtabon is a beach that splits west off the road toward the Underground River, so some travelers plan half a day at each on the same day. However, the beach has almost no electricity or mobile signal and no ATM, so bring cash, water and snacks. Most prices in this guide come from 2019~2020 travel blogs, so please check them again locally.

With no cluster of hotels, it is quiet, and coconut trees stand along the shore. Many reports say there are almost no people on weekdays, which makes it good for reading or walking the beach. Be aware that the sand is not especially white.
About
after turning off the highway toward the beach, guides mention a viewpoint with a view over the whole beach. It is a good place to stop the motorbike and take photos before going down.
Because the coast faces west, several reports say you can watch the sky turn red at dusk. However, the road back is dark with few streetlights, so plan your travel time after sunset.
Guides mention plates of grilled fish, chicken or pork at about
and a coconut at about
. Pay the cottage rental (
) and eat in the shade, and it is enough for a relaxing half day.
You can take a small boat to Chicken Island, about
15 minutes
away, and a 2020 guide gives about
round trip. Waves and boat service vary from day to day, so ask when you arrive.

In the season when waves are high, some people surf and skimboard here. You must bring your own equipment, and since the same period carries a warning about a high risk of drowning, judge it separately from swimming.
Renting a motorbike in the city for about
a day and riding to the beach is a known option. The road is mostly paved but has some bumpy sections, so we recommend it only for confident riders.

items.title: Half-day route
items.subtitle: Leave in the morning and return after lunch

children.text: Leave Puerto Princesa by motorbike or van. Take the highway north and turn onto the beach road near the
23 km
marker.
Look over the whole scene from the viewpoint at the beach entrance and go down. If there is an entrance fee, pay it at the entrance and pick a cottage first.
Swim in the shallows or walk along the beach. On days with high waves, do not go into deep water.
Have lunch of grilled fish or chicken at a cottage. Orders tend to come slowly, so order as soon as you arrive.
If the weather is good, ask about a boat to Chicken Island or rest in the shade.
Head back to the city before sunset. If you stay until sunset, be ready for the dark road home.
If you use public transport, transfers take longer, so set aside at least half a day.

items.title: Sunset route
items.subtitle: Go in the afternoon, watch the sunset and return

children.text: Leave the city for the beach. It takes about
40~50 minutes
by motorbike.
Pick a cottage and walk the beach or rest with a coconut.
Watch the sunset along the shoreline. The coast faces west, so you can see the sun sink into the sea.
Head out to the highway before it gets dark. The road has few lights, so a good headlight and a backup light help.
Sunset time changes with the season, so check that day's sunset time first.
There are direct flights from Manila to Puerto Princesa Airport (PPS), and the flight takes about
1 hour 30 minutes
The airport is inside the city, so you can get from the airport to downtown briefly by tricycle or taxi. One guide gives the distance from the airport to the beach as about
34 km

items.title: By motorbike or car from downtown

children.text: This is the most common way. Guides say to take the national highway north from the city, turn onto the branch toward the beach near the
23 km
marker, and turn left after about
10 minutes
to reach the beach.
A 2019 guide gives motorbike rental at about
a day. Check licence and local rules before you go.
Near the beach there are narrow, bumpy sections.

items.title: By bus and tricycle from San Jose Terminal

children.text: Go from downtown to San Jose Terminal and take a bus toward El Nido, Sabang or Roxas. Get off at Bacungan; guides give the fare as about
and the trip as about
30 minutes
From Bacungan a tricycle takes about
15 minutes
to the beach, and one guide gives
per tricycle (up to 3 people).
Return transport may run out, so ask the tricycle driver to wait or get a contact number.
A 2020 guide gives a round-trip chartered van from the city at about
for 1~10 people. One way takes about
50 minutes
, and 8 hours of use was included, with extra hours at
each.
With a larger group, the cost per person drops, and it is safer and more comfortable than a motorbike.
Puerto Princesa generally has a wet season from May to December and a dry season from January to April. The average annual temperature is about
. However, Nagtabon is on the west coast and is affected by the monsoon winds.

Travel reports warn that waves are strongest and drowning incidents have occurred during the Amihan season, October to February, and that big waves also hit during the rainy-season monsoon. So if swimming is your goal, consider March to May, relatively dry months, but in any month ask locals about the sea conditions when you arrive.

The beach has no resort; guides describe only cottages run by locals and a few bungalows. One guide says a bungalow has two floors with mosquito nets and generator power in the evening, and few people stay more than two days. Do not expect much from the sleeping and shower facilities; most visitors stay in Puerto Princesa and make a day trip. Camping is not common now because cottages line the shore, and one report says to ask permission before pitching a tent.
You eat at the cottage eateries on the beach. A plate of grilled fish, chicken or pork with rice is about
, and guides mention a liter of beer at about

. These are old figures, so check before you order. The menu is limited, so bringing a packed lunch, water and snacks is reassuring. Do your shopping and wider dining in Puerto Princesa city before you go.
Withdraw cash in the city beforehand. There is no ATM near the beach, and most cottages accept only cash.
Mobile signal and electricity are unreliable. Save the map offline and bring a power bank.
The turnoffs on the way to the beach are confusing, so it helps to read directions in advance, such as the
23 km
marker, a big tree and a school, and a gas station and shop.
If you plan to stay until sunset, allow plenty of time to return and choose a motorbike or vehicle with a working headlight.
Choose a cottage as soon as you arrive and confirm the rental fee. The beach has little shade, so without a cottage midday is hard.
The sun is strong even outside summer, so bring sunscreen, a hat and a large towel.
If you go out to Chicken Island, agree the boat fare and number of people first and ask for life jackets.
On days with high waves, it is right not to swim. If in doubt, ask a local first.
During the Amihan season, October to February, waves are strong and drowning incidents have been reported. Check local conditions before swimming and do not go into deep water.
We could not find any guide saying that lifeguards are stationed at the beach. If you go with children, keep your eyes on them.
Some reports say the sand is not very white and the coral is not colorful, so do not expect a snorkeling hotspot.
Electricity and mobile signal are unreliable, so contacting help in an emergency is difficult. Share your travel plan with your group.
The highway and village roads are dark after evening. If you ride a motorbike, it is safer to return before sunset.
Many fees and rules come from old guides. Check the latest notices and local conditions, and contact the Puerto Princesa City tourism office if needed.
A national park about
50 km
north of the city, reached by the same national highway as Nagtabon. Combining both in one day requires an early start.
An island-hopping area in the sea east of the city, on the opposite side from west-coast Nagtabon, so it is hard to combine on the same day. Split them across different days.
The base city with the airport, terminal, accommodation and restaurants. After visiting the beach, it is easier to have dinner and rest in the city.
A small island about
15 minutes
from the beach by small boat. Boat fare and whether boats run are decided locally.
